intro: The Republic of the Congo, also called Congo-Brazzaville, lies across the Congo River from its larger neighbour, DR Congo.

chapters.title: Kongo and Loango
text: The Kingdom of Loango on the coast and parts of the Kongo and Teke kingdoms traded ivory, copper and, later, enslaved people with Europeans.

chapters.title: French Congo
text: Explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signed a treaty with the Teke king in 1880, and Brazzaville was named after him. During World War Two, Brazzaville was the capital of Free France in Africa.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Congo became independent in 1960. It was a Marxist state from 1969 to 1991. Civil wars in the 1990s were followed by the return of Denis Sassou Nguesso, who has ruled for most years since 1979.

keyTerms.meaning: A name used to tell it apart from DR Congo.
